jurisdictions.name: Fargo
notes: Residential permit applications are submitted through the city's online permit portal, where plan reviewers send status updates by email.
The city's FAQ says private pools holding more than 24 in. of water must be surrounded by a fence or barrier at least 48 in. tall, set at least 4 ft from the outside of the pool.
Gates in the pool barrier must be self-closing and self-latching, and the FAQ cites City of Fargo Ordinance No 5425.
The city lists local amendments to the 2024 International Building Code on its code requirements page.

jurisdictions.name: West Fargo
jurisdictions.office: City of West Fargo Building Inspections
notes: A building permit is required before building or placing a pool, spa or hot tub with water deeper than 2 ft, and an inspection is required when the installation is finished.
The pool guideline says applicants apply in the online portal using the Residential - New Accessory Structure / Shed sub type and upload a digital site plan.
The site plan must show lot lines and easements, existing buildings, pool dimensions and distances to property lines, fence and gate locations, and any new paving.
The city adopts a local amendment of International Property Maintenance Code section 303 for pool barriers, with the top at least 48 in. above grade for pools deeper than 24 in.
